statement: The real installed codebase-memory-mcp baseline (v0.8.1) is at C:\Users\sujan.mishra\AppData\Local\Programs\codebase-memory-mcp\codebase-memory-mcp.exe and its `cli <tool> <json>` CLI mode is drivable directly, but its JSON arg parser rejects unescaped backslashes in string values -- any Windows path passed as a JSON string value (e.g. repo_path) must be forward-slash-normalized first, or the parser silently reports the required field as missing even though the key is present.
why: Spent significant probe time getting `repo_path is required` errors from index_repository despite passing a correct key -- root cause was backslash-in-JSON-string breaking the baseline's own JSON parser, not a wrong param name.
howToApply: Any future baseline CLI driver (this lane's crates/enforcer-memory/tests/feature_parity/baseline.rs::CliDriver) must normalize every path value to forward slashes before building the request JSON string.

statement: First live tool-by-tool parity diff against the real codebase-memory-mcp baseline ran successfully: 13 tools compared, 5 equal, 1 better (get_code_snippet's sha256 hash), 1 worse (trace_path calls -- candidate trace_calls did not find the expected outbound callee on the fixture repo, root cause not yet isolated), 2 incomparable (list_projects and search_graph bm25 use structurally different mechanisms), 4 unrunnable (query_graph has no Cypher module in enforcer-memory yet; manage_adr has no project-scoped whole-document get/update; index_status and search_code need additional plumbing this pass didn't build). Proof artifacts: proof/memory/x06-kg-parity.json, proof/memory/x06-parity/tool-results.ndjson, proof/memory/x06-parity/tool-diffs.ndjson.
why: This is the first real (non-fabricated) evidence of where enforcer-memory's landed library functions do and do not match the C baseline's actual behavior on identical fixture data.
howToApply: Future x06 lanes closing the query_graph/manage_adr/index_status/search_code gaps should re-run `cargo test -p enforcer-memory --test feature_parity_harness -- --ignored run_live_parity_comparison_and_emit_proof` to update this parity picture; the trace_path(calls) worse-verdict deserves a follow-up investigation into whether TraceDirection::Out or the node-id lookup in analysis::trace::trace_calls is the mismatch.

statement: When multiple parallel lanes are actively landing files under crates/enforcer-memory/src/**, a test-only lane's cargo build can fail transiently with errors that are entirely someone else's in-flight work (missing module files, unresolved crates, duplicate definitions) -- these transient failures are not the test-only lane's bug and should not be fixed by editing src/** (out of scope); the correct move is to poll until src/** stabilizes, then re-run the build, and only debug remaining errors that are actually inside the test-only lane's own files.
why: Hit exactly this: cargo build -p enforcer-memory --tests failed first with 8 errors (missing redaction.rs, unresolved ed25519_dalek/zstd/rand_core, duplicate from_digest), then with 18 errors on a retry as other lanes kept editing, then dropped to 2 (both mine: missing Debug derive) once src/** landed.
howToApply: A test-only worker should mail a BLOCKED status with the exact error signature when this happens, keep holding file claims, and retry the build periodically rather than attempting to patch someone else's in-flight src/** module.
